p.src:
Begin with a lattice of small magnets. Each spin can point up or down, and neighboring spins lower their energy by pointing in the same direction. On a three-dimensional cubic lattice a spin has six nearest neighbors, but the precise coordination number is not important. What matters is the rule $E_{\parallel}<E_{\rm antiparallel}.$ The microscopic rule is unchanged if every spin is reversed: $\uparrow\longleftrightarrow\downarrow.$ Nevertheless, the lowest-energy configurations are not individually symmetric. They are $\{\uparrow\uparrow\uparrow\cdots\},
  \qquad
  \{\downarrow\downarrow\downarrow\cdots\}.$ The equations allow both, but a cold macroscopic sample must choose one.

p.src: Without the external bias, up and down have the same bulk energy. The lowest-energy constrained state then contains an up domain, a down domain, and a finite transition layer between them. This interface is a domain wall, the characteristic defect of this broken discrete symmetry.

\end{aligned}$ The relativistic shorthand in $\mathcal L$ contains the positive time-derivative term and negative spatial-gradient term; the Hamiltonian energy density has both contributions positive.

p.src:
Fix $\phi=+f$ on one side of a sample and $\phi=-f$ on the other. The field cannot jump without cost, because $E_{\rm wall}
  =\int dx\left[
      \frac12\left(\frac{d\phi}{dx}\right)^2+V(\phi)-V(f)
    \right].$ An abrupt jump makes $d\phi/dx$ enormous. The minimum-energy wall therefore spreads the change over a finite width, balancing gradient energy against the potential cost of passing between the minima. The familiar kink solution for the potential in Eq. [eq:l07-double-well] is $\phi_{\rm wall}(x)
  =f\tanh\!\left[f\sqrt{\frac{\lambda}{2}}\,(x-x_0)\right],$ an explicit realization of the smooth transition described at the board.  (Editorial clarification: The lecture argues from the shape of the potential and the gradient term but does not solve the field equation. Equation [eq:l07-kink] is included as the standard solution of that stated model, making the qualitative wall concrete without changing the argument.)

  =-a\,\phi^*\phi+b(\phi^*\phi)^2,

p.src:
Write the broken complex field as $\phi(x)=\rho(x)e^{i\alpha(x)}.$ Both $\rho$ and $\alpha$ are fields. Differentiation gives $\begin{aligned}\partial_\mu\phi
  &=e^{i\alpha}
    \left(\partial_\mu\rho+i\rho\,\partial_\mu\alpha\right),\\
  \partial_\mu\phi^*
  &=e^{-i\alpha}
    \left(\partial_\mu\rho-i\rho\,\partial_\mu\alpha\right).\end{aligned}$ The cross terms cancel, leaving $\partial_\mu\phi^*\,\partial^\mu\phi
  =(\partial_\mu\rho)(\partial^\mu\rho)
   +\rho^2(\partial_\mu\alpha)(\partial^\mu\alpha).$ Since $\phi^*\phi=\rho^2$, $\mathcal L
  =(\partial\rho)^2+\rho^2(\partial\alpha)^2-V(\rho^2).$ The potential contains $\rho$ but not $\alpha$. That absence is the symmetry in its most useful form.

The new question is whether $\phi'(x)=e^{i\theta(x)}\phi(x)$ can be a symmetry when $\theta$ varies arbitrarily through spacetime. The function $\theta(x)$ is a transformation parameter, not an additional dynamical field. We test the proposal by differentiating: $\partial_\mu\phi'
  =e^{i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi+i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi\right].$ The extra term was absent for constant $\theta$. For the conjugate, $\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}
  =e^{-i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi^*-i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi^*\right].$ Their product is $\begin{aligned}\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}\partial^\mu\phi'
  ={}&
  \partial_\mu\phi^*\partial^\mu\phi
  i\left(
      \phi\,\partial_\mu\phi^*
      -\phi^*\partial_\mu\phi
    \right)\partial^\mu\theta
  \nonumber\\
  &+\phi^*\phi\,
    \partial_\mu\theta\,\partial^\mu\theta.
  \end{aligned}$ The potential remains invariant because $\phi^*\phi$ does, but the ordinary kinetic term fails. A global symmetry has not automatically become a local one.

新しい問いは、$\phi'(x)=e^{i\theta(x)}\phi(x)$が、$\theta$が時空を通じて任意に変化するときに対称性であり得るか、というものである。関数$\theta(x)$は変換パラメータであり、追加の力学場ではない。この提案を微分によって検証する：$\partial_\mu\phi'
  =e^{i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi+i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi\right].$。この余分な項は、$\theta$が定数のときには存在しなかった。共役については、$\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}
  =e^{-i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi^*-i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi^*\right].$。これらの積は$\begin{aligned}\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}\partial^\mu\phi'
  ={}&
  \partial_\mu\phi^*\partial^\mu\phi
  i\left(
      \phi\,\partial_\mu\phi^*
      -\phi^*\partial_\mu\phi
    \right)\partial^\mu\theta
  \nonumber\\
  &+\phi^*\phi\,
    \partial_\mu\theta\,\partial^\mu\theta.
  \end{aligned}$である。ポテンシャルは$\phi^*\phi$が不変であるため不変のままだが、通常の運動項は失敗する。大域的対称性は自動的に局所的対称性になったわけではない。

  =e^{i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi+i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi\right].$ 当$\theta$为常数时，这一额外项不存在。对于共轭场， $\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}
  =e^{-i\theta}
   \left[\partial_\mu\phi^*-i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi^*\right].$ 两者之积为 $\begin{aligned}\partial_\mu\phi^{*\prime}\partial^\mu\phi'
  ={}&
  \partial_\mu\phi^*\partial^\mu\phi
  i\left(
      \phi\,\partial_\mu\phi^*
      -\phi^*\partial_\mu\phi
    \right)\partial^\mu\theta
  \nonumber\\
  &+\phi^*\phi\,
    \partial_\mu\theta\,\partial^\mu\theta.
  \end{aligned}$ 势能项仍然不变，因为$\phi^*\phi$不变，但普通的动能项不再成立。全局对称性并没有自动变成局域对称性。

For the conjugate field, $D_\mu\phi^*=\partial_\mu\phi^*-iA_\mu\phi^*.$ Now $\begin{aligned}D'_\mu\phi'
  &=
  \left(\partial_\mu+iA'_\mu\right)e^{i\theta}\phi
  \nonumber\\
  &=
  e^{i\theta}
  \left[
    \partial_\mu\phi+i(\partial_\mu\theta)\phi
    +i(A_\mu-\partial_\mu\theta)\phi
  \right]
  \nonumber\\
  &=e^{i\theta}D_\mu\phi.

p.src: The next step is to use the broken potential of Eq. [eq:l07-mexican-hat] inside the gauge-invariant theory of Eq. [eq:l07-scalar-qed]. Then two things happen together: the separate Goldstone particle disappears from the physical spectrum, and the vector field acquires a mass. In the usual pedagogical language the gauge symmetry is spontaneously broken; more precisely, the gauge redundancy remains while the theory enters a Higgs phase with a massive vector excitation.  (Editorial clarification: A local gauge symmetry is a redundancy of description rather than an ordinary physical symmetry acting between distinct observable states.
